descriptionChirho: Filled to capacity with a substance, quality, or condition; physically or spiritually replete. Used of baskets full of fragments (Mk 8:19), Stephen full of grace (Acts 6:8), or a person full of leprosy (Lk 5:12). Translations uniformly render as 'filled up': eng 'full,' spa 'lleno/llenos,' arb مَمْلُوءٌ (mamluu, filled), hin भरा हुआ (bhara hua, filled up), kor 가득 찬 (gadeuk chan, brimming), swa 'amejaa/vimejaa' (filled, overflowing).

Entire or complete in degree, lacking nothing; used of a full reward (2 Jn 1:8) where the emphasis is on completeness rather than physical content. Translations diverge toward 'completeness': eng 'full,' spa 'plena' (plenary), arb كامِلاً (kamilan, complete/perfect), hin पूर्ण (purna, whole/complete), kor 온전한 (onjeonhan, perfect/intact), swa 'kamili' (complete, perfect). This sense overlaps with τέλειος in the domain of wholeness and totality.
